I am 75 years old and have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 55 years. My wife and I are the only ones left at home, so we keep things simple and stick to what we know works. The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. Now that it is turning green, I will topdress it with about 45 jin of urea per mu and give it the first irrigation from my well. The wheat needs three irrigations in total: one now at green-up, one at jointing, and one at grain-filling. I will also spray once for weeds, twice for insects, and once for rust or scab—that makes four sprayings in total. Before sowing wheat each year I use the rotary tiller, and I always use improved seed varieties like Jimai 22 from the village supply shop. For fertilizer, besides the urea topdressing, I put down about 100 jin per mu of compound fertilizer as a basal dose, which gives the crop plenty of nitrogen, phosphate, and potash.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately sow the summer mazie. At my age I do not bother with deep tillage for mazie—I plant directly into the stubble to save labor and time. I use hybrid seed, usually Denghai 605, because it gives good yields. I apply about 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer at planting, and that is usually enough nitrogen and potash for the season. I will irrigate twice if the summer is dry, especially at the big trumpet stage. For pests, I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for corn borers, so three applications total. I know my land well, and if I manage it this way, I expect about 500 kg per mu of wheat and about 550 kg per mu of mazie.
